prompt: 002 Einkaufsliste ist gegroomt. Entwirf das technische Design dafür.
assertions: Asks no questions: the final message contains no question to the user, no options to choose from and no request to review or approve
Traceability: every story/acceptance criterion and every business rule of the target requirements document is mapped to a concrete design element
No open decisions: the design contains no TBD/TODO, no 'either X or Y' left to developers, no unresolved 'consider'/'if needed' choices
Out-of-scope items of the target requirements are not designed or built
Data model given with entities, fields and types; API/interfaces given with method, path and request/response shape
All written files are in English

Detects the conflict between the stakeholder's 'Sync am besten über Firebase' and the product constraint that FE+BE+DB run on the Pi, and documents it openly (both requirements, resolution, what is lost) instead of silently picking one
The conflict resolution is flagged for later stakeholder confirmation (e.g. a change request for the groomer) without blocking the design
Builds on the existing stack (Ktor, PostgreSQL, React PWA, Caddy) without adding a new database or runtime
Addresses that the Pi is currently reachable only in the home network while the list is used in the supermarket over mobile data, and decides how the phone reaches the backend there
Live updates between household members use a concrete mechanism (e.g. SSE or WebSocket) including reconnect/resync behaviour
Offline viewing and ticking: changes are queued locally and replayed; conflicts (e.g. line deleted or shopping finished while offline) have defined outcomes
Merge rules R1/R2/R2a/R2b are specified precisely (case-insensitive name + same unit, only open recipe lines, quantity-less ingredients, free items never merged)
Area assignment is specified: household corrections take priority, then a concrete built-in mapping, fallback Sonstiges; corrections stored household-wide
The memory/capacity budget of the Pi is re-checked after adding the feature (e.g. long-lived connections)
Design plans a docker-compose stack in which every server-side component (frontend serving, backend, database, workers) is a service, and 'docker compose up -d' starts the whole product
Every compose service has its image/build, ports, named volumes for persistent data, env/secrets via .env with .env.example, healthcheck, depends_on and restart policy specified
